title: Personal data and LGPD
subtitle: Keep only what is needed, for a short time and with a written reason: minimization, retention and legal basis
mission: Aurora’s assistant records every conversation to audit and improve. About 2,000 a week, and around 21% carry personal data: CPF in 7%, e-mail in 6%, phone in 5% and health data in 3% (medical certificate, medicine, appointment). The data protection officer (DPO) accepts at most 1,000 conversations with personal data exposed in a breach of the log database. Choose what to redact before recording, how many days to keep and which legal basis justifies keeping, and see the size of the possible damage.

why.simples:
The best way not to leak a piece of data is not to have it. If the conversation is recorded with the CPF replaced by [CPF], whoever steals the file takes only a pile of brackets. And what you do record, how long do you keep it? Like the fridge: everything has a shelf life, and whoever forgets ends up with a problem at the back of the shelf.
Brazilian law asks, in short, for three things: a clear reason to keep (the legal basis), keeping only what is necessary for that reason and deleting when the reason ends. And the person may ask to see, correct or delete what you hold about them.
why.dev:
Minimization in code: redact before recording (log, trace, evaluation set, analytics), not after. Regex handles fixed formats: CPF (check the verification digits so you do not redact any 11-digit number), e-mail and phone. Health data, names and addresses in free text need a model-based detector (the lesson’s "health" option uses a classifier); that detector also errs, so redact in two passes and measure on real cases.
Retention: define the period per purpose (audit, quality, security), record the reason and enforce it with a job that deletes (the recipe’s code). Identification: record a code instead of the name (a pseudonym with a key kept apart) so you can find and delete one person’s data when they ask. Pseudonymizing is not anonymizing: if it can be reversed with reasonable means, it is still personal data.
What goes to a provider’s API counts too: send only what is needed and, if the provider is outside Brazil, check with legal whether there is an international transfer. Record who the data is shared with.
why.especialista:
This lesson is general information about the law, not legal advice: validate each decision with your company’s legal team and data protection officer.
Law 13,709/2018 (LGPD). Art. 6 requires good faith and ten principles (purpose, adequacy, necessity, free access, data quality, transparency, security, prevention, non-discrimination, accountability); minimization is the necessity principle, limiting processing to the minimum necessary. Art. 7 lists ten grounds (legal bases) for personal data, among them consent, compliance with a legal obligation, performance of a contract and legitimate interest; art. 5, XII defines consent as a free, informed and unambiguous manifestation for a specific purpose, which deserves care when the one asking is the employer. Data about health, racial or ethnic origin, religious belief, political opinion, union membership and genetic or biometric data are sensitive (art. 5, II) and may only be processed under the hypotheses of art. 11, a list of its own: specific and prominent consent, or cases such as legal obligation, regular exercise of rights and health protection. Legitimate interest is not on that list.
End of processing and deletion are in arts. 15 and 16 (with exceptions, such as compliance with a legal obligation). The data subject’s rights are in art. 18: confirmation of processing, access, correction, anonymization, blocking or deletion of unnecessary data, portability, deletion of data processed with consent, information about sharing and withdrawal of consent. Art. 46 requires technical and administrative security measures, and art. 48 requires notifying incidents to the ANPD and the data subject; Resolution CD/ANPD 15/2024 sets three business days from the moment of knowing the incident affected personal data. Art. 33 limits international transfers (the ANPD approved the regulation in Resolution 19/2024, with standard contractual clauses). A simple fine can reach 2% of revenue (art. 52, II).
The ANPD has already acted on AI: in July 2024 it ordered the suspension of Meta’s new privacy policy in Brazil, which would have allowed using users’ data to train generative AI, and on 30 August 2024 it suspended the measure after approving a compliance plan, with individual notice and an opt-out.

data.detectorSys: You detect personal data in messages to Aurora’s HR assistant. For each type, say true if it appears in the message and false if not: cpf, email, phone and health (any health information: medical certificate, illness, medicine, appointment). Reply only with JSON: {"cpf":false,"email":false,"phone":false,"health":false}.

steps:
Run:
python pii.py
The CPF and e-mail of the first message and the phone of the second come out as [CPF], [EMAIL] and [TELEFONE]. The "son’s medical certificate" is still there: free-text health data needs a classifier, like the lesson’s.

Create log_store.py: records only the redacted text, enforces retention and handles one person’s deletion request (schedule purge_old_logs() in a daily cron):
import json
import pathlib
import time

from pii import pseudonym, redact

RETENTION_DAYS = 90  # a política da Aurora para logs de auditoria; registre o motivo e quem aprovou


def log_conversation(user_id, question, answer, day):
    """Grava só texto redigido e o código do colaborador, num arquivo por dia."""
    path = pathlib.Path("logs") / f"{day}.jsonl"
    path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    row = {"user": pseudonym(user_id), "question": redact(question), "answer": redact(answer)}
    with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


def purge_old_logs(now=None):
    """Roda todo dia (cron): apaga o que passou do prazo. Retenção que ninguém executa não existe."""
    limit = (now or time.time()) - RETENTION_DAYS * 86400
    removed = 0
    for f in pathlib.Path("logs").glob("*.jsonl"):
        if f.stat().st_mtime < limit:
            f.unlink()
            removed += 1
    return removed


def erase_person(user_id):
    """Pedido de eliminação do titular (art. 18, VI): reescreve os arquivos sem as linhas dele."""
    code = pseudonym(user_id)
    for f in pathlib.Path("logs").glob("*.jsonl"):
        rows = [r for r in f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if json.loads(r)["user"] != code]
        f.write_text("\n".join(rows) + ("\n" if rows else ""), encoding="utf-8")

Write a short document for the data protection officer to review: purpose of the log, chosen legal basis and who approved it, the 90-day period and why, types of data that may still appear and who the data is shared with (including the model provider).
recipe.ok: pii.py prints the three messages with [CPF], [EMAIL] and [TELEFONE] in place of the data and a 16-character code for the employee; log_store.py records only redacted text in logs/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl, deletes files older than 90 days and removes one person’s rows with erase_person().
